programme: AIP, ESRRA and NR2C2 converge on the ESR1 locus and canonical estrogen-response genes — AIP and ESRRA both list ESR1, GREB1/TFF1-class targets directly, and NR2C2 also targets ESR1 alongside CCND1/AKT1/TERT. ESRRA additionally runs the PGC1A-linked oxidative/mitochondrial metabolic programme (PPARGC1A, PPARA, PCK1, GK, PDK4), while HDAC5 represses glucose-transporter and growth-factor genes (SLC2A1, SLC2A4, FGF2, WT1) in the same hormonal-metabolic circuit, and PML adds p53/SUMO-dependent surveillance (TP53, CDKN1A) that in ovarian cancer has been tied to control of chemosensitivity via MYC.
role_in_a: Not documented anywhere in this record — no Open Targets association and no on-topic paper for any of these five factors in fibromyalgia. If this axis operates in fibromyalgia at all, it would be expected to show as altered estrogen-responsive and mitochondrial/oxidative-metabolism gene expression in blood, consistent with the field's general (but here unretrieved) hypotheses about estrogen fluctuation and mitochondrial dysfunction in fibromyalgia — this is inference, not something the material supports.
role_in_b: Reasonably well placed: ESRRA copy-number variation tracks with ovarian cancer histological subtype (PMID 33751740); NR2C2 transcriptionally drives NAA30 to promote ovarian cancer progression (PMID 41615304); HDAC5 sits in an IL-6/paclitaxel-resistance axis (PMID 40112929) and a HIF-1α tumorigenicity axis (PMID 34990588); PML/SUMOylation intersects MYC to shape drug sensitivity (PMID 40487451). Together these point to the module supporting proliferation and chemoresistance in ovarian cancer specifically, not cancer in general.
shared_axis: Both conditions are strongly female-predominant, and each has been separately proposed (though not documented here) to involve estrogen-linked and mitochondrial/metabolic dysregulation — fibromyalgia through pain-sensitization hypotheses tied to hormonal state, ovarian cancer through ERRalpha/estrogen-receptor-driven proliferation. No source in this record connects the two diseases through this axis directly.
reasoning: The ESR1/ESRRA-PGC1A module is nameable from the factors' own target sets and four of the five carrying factors are independently placed in ovarian cancer by on-point papers, but nothing here places any of them in fibromyalgia — Open Targets is null and every retrieved paper for fibromyalgia-side factors is off-topic. The disease link therefore rests on general reasoning about female-predominant, hormone-associated conditions rather than on anything retrieved, which is the definition of moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 33751740 — ESRRA copy-number variation is associated with ovarian cancer histological subtype. PMID 41615304 — NR2C2 transcriptionally regulates NAA30, promoting ovarian cancer progression. PMID 40112929 — HDAC5, via H1.0, modulates IL-6 expression and paclitaxel resistance in ovarian cancer cells. PMID 34990588 — miR-671-5p suppresses HDAC5 and HIF-1α to reduce ovarian cancer tumorigenicity. PMID 40487451 — SUMOylation (PML pathway) intersects MYC to shape drug sensitivity/resistance in ovarian cancer. None found placing AIP, or any of these five factors, in fibromyalgia.
how_to_falsify: In ovarian cancer lines, co-deplete ESRRA and NR2C2 and test whether ESR1/GREB1/TFF1 and the PPARGC1A-driven mitochondrial gene set move together, confirming the proposed convergence; separately, profile PBMCs or muscle biopsies from a fibromyalgia cohort versus matched controls for coordinated shifts in this same ESR1/PGC1A gene set — if no coordinated change appears in the fibromyalgia tissue relative to controls, the shared axis does not hold and the pairing is spurious.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (fibromyalgia) versus ovary (ovarian cancer) — very different contexts, so 'concordant target sets' reflects network-inferred TF-target agreement, not confirmed co-expression in matched tissue. 64 patient-group comparisons were available but only 2 independent cohort pairs, limiting independent replication. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed STAT1, FOXO1, FOXO3, IRF8 and other interferon/immune master regulators, which is why no generic immune story is being told here; the single-view exclusion list (ZNF384, PREB, RORA, etc.) rules out any account resting on one patient subgroup. The fibromyalgia side of this account is entirely unevidenced in the record and should be read as a hypothesis to test, not a finding.
